title: ResultSafe Core risk register
summary: Risk register governing contract extraction, identity, projection ownership, multi-language parity, publication, and truthful qualification.

items.title: Canonizing implementation bugs
items.description: Literal extraction from TypeScript could convert accidental matcher and refiner defects into normative behavior.
items.mitigation: Classify audited behavior as intended contract, projection detail, compatibility deviation, or defect before approval.

items.title: UUID ordering misuse
items.description: UUIDv7 timestamp bits could be misused as authoritative order, time, authorization, or tenant boundary.
items.mitigation: Require explicit timestamp, revision, sequence, authority, and tenant fields and validate their independent use.

items.title: Dual canonical authority
items.description: JSON, TypeScript, Markdown, or SQLite could independently claim canonical behavior and drift.
items.mitigation: Make strict JSON the sole authority and reject reverse writes or untracked generated differences.

items.title: Cross-language semantic drift
items.description: Language-specific APIs may silently diverge in branch behavior, exceptions, async order, and type guarantees.
items.mitigation: Generate adapters from one scenario catalog and require projection-specific conformance evidence.

items.title: SQLite becomes authority
items.description: Operational convenience could lead consumers to mutate the generated database as a canonical registry.
items.mitigation: Publish read-only artifacts, prohibit reverse projection, and rebuild through staged deterministic compilation.

items.title: Tenant overlay contamination
items.description: Tenant-owned annotations or evidence could be mixed into the immutable public contract database.
items.mitigation: Separate immutable core and operational overlay databases and enforce tenant-qualified PK, FK, and query predicates.

items.title: Fabricated publication authority
items.description: Local code could reuse or invent AASDVGS PackageFamilyId, ReleaseId, or PNID values.
items.mitigation: Keep admission external, evidence-bound, and blocked until the owning authority allocates publication identity.

items.title: Unexecuted work reported as pass
items.description: Structural validation or generated scenarios could be presented as behavioral, security, or reliability proof.
items.mitigation: Keep status classes independent and enforce NOT_EXECUTED and DEFERRED semantics in schemas and validators.

items.title: Portable Failure data disclosure
items.description: Messages, details, causes, metadata, or extensions could disclose secrets, stack traces, process paths, credentials, or private tenant data across a boundary.
items.mitigation: Treat optional facets as public-boundary data, prohibit runtime exceptions and stacks, apply explicit redaction, and preserve only version and code when stripping presentation.

items.title: Cause topology loss
items.description: A codec or adapter could flatten, reorder, reassociate, deduplicate, or cycle recursive Cause nodes and silently alter failure semantics.
items.mitigation: Validate exact binary structure, child order, acyclicity, and resource bounds with executable scenarios and strict matrix cells.

items.title: Effect compatibility overclaim
items.description: Semantic similarity could be misrepresented as representation identity or as implemented Python and Effect runtime interoperability.
items.mitigation: Record semantic mappings only, reject silent loss, and retain PLANNED status for targets without executable APIs.

items.title: Public module artifact drift
items.description: Root exports, direct subpaths, declarations, ESM, CJS, and packed manifest targets can diverge when generated artifact paths are maintained independently.
items.mitigation: Use one normative source-to-artifact derivation and require exhaustive isolated packed consumers for the registered module surface.

items.title: Implicit codec policy
items.description: Codec behavior could be mistaken for core representation identity or accepted without executing malformed-vector rejection and topology-preservation evidence.
items.mitigation: Keep codecs in the separate package, register exact vectors and peer policy, and require final artifact-bound package qualification.

items.title: Effect adapter version drift
items.description: Effect API or semantic changes could invalidate mappings if compatibility is claimed beyond the exact version exercised by the separate adapter.
items.mitigation: Declare Effect 3.22.1 exactly, bind executable evidence to the adapter package, and rerun the atomic adapter gate for every supported-version change.
